# Fabrication and errors in the bibliographic citations generated by ChatGPT (Walters & Wilder, 2023)

- **Source:** Scientific Reports 13: 14045 · https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-41032-5 (pages = PDF pages)
- **File:** `../papers/walters-2023-fabrication-errors-chatgpt-citations.pdf`
- **Licence:** CC BY 4.0.
- **Evidence:** empirical · 636 citations in short literature reviews on 42 topics, checked by hand (p. 1–3).

## What it says
- 55% of GPT-3.5 citations and 18% of GPT-4 citations were fabricated; 43% and 24% of the real ones had
  substantive errors (p. 1).
- Fabricated citations look legitimate at first glance, and the model often answers wrongly when asked whether a
  citation is correct (p. 2).

## What it means for the plugin
- Supports "never invent a citation": every reference must come from a search result or a file read.
- A model checking its own citations is not a check; verification must look the work up in a database (DOI).
- Newer models fabricate less, not never: verification stays necessary.

## Quotes
- "Within this set of documents, 55% of the GPT-3.5 citations but just 18% of the GPT-4 citations are fabricated." (p. 1)
